Days Of The New.biography: Days of the New is an American rock band from Charlestown, Indiana, formed in 1995. The band consists of vocalist/guitarist Travis Meeks and a variety of supporting musicians. They are best known for the hit singles "Touch, Peel and Stand", "The Down Town", "Shelf in the Room", and "Enemy".

perplexity.description:
Days of the New (1997) stands as the debut album from the Indiana rock band of the same name, released on June 3, 1997 through Outpost Recordings. Recorded in October and November 1996 at Woodland Studios in Nashville under producer Scott Litt—known for his work with R.E.M. and Nirvana—the album showcases a distinctive dark acoustic rock sound that set the band apart from their contemporaries. The twelve-track collection, frequently referred to as the "Yellow" or "Orange" album after its cover design, features songs written entirely by lead vocalist and guitarist Travis Meeks, establishing his songwriting as the creative foundation of the project.

The album achieved significant commercial success, selling 1.5 million copies worldwide and earning platinum certification in the United States. Three singles from the record became mainstream hits: "Touch, Peel and Stand" reached number one on Billboard's Rock Chart and was later named the "Greatest of All-Time Mainstream Rock Song" by Billboard, while "The Down Town" and "Shelf in the Room" both achieved top 40 status. The fresh acoustic approach combined with Meeks' catchy vocal hooks resonated strongly with audiences in 1997, establishing the band as a notable presence in the alternative rock landscape of that era.

The album's influence has proven enduring, maintaining its relevance across the two decades following its initial release. It marked the beginning of what would become the band's signature practice of releasing self-titled albums distinguished by color—a pattern that continued with subsequent releases. The success of this debut positioned Days of the New as significant contributors to the late-1990s rock scene, though internal tensions would lead to the original band's dissolution in 1999, shortly after an ill-fated tour with Metallica and Jerry Cantrell.
